landforms.method: noise render; relief (max - min) at ~16/64/256-block windows, topographic position at 256

crossCheck.method: noise render surface (one above the first motion-blocking block from the top or the roof's underside) against the generated column's first solid-to-air boundary below the top or the roof

vertical.definitions: runs of collision blocks; runs closer than 16 form one block; the lowest block's top is the surface, tops above it are sky; overhang: an air pocket within 16 of the top block's top; cave: a pocket of 3+ deeper in the surface block; roofed: under the dimension's ceiling

surface.note: shares are % of all sampled columns; 'top' is the highest non-air block above the surface (leaves, plants, snow, liquids count), 'ground' the surface block itself

vegetation.method: trees are 26-connected components of log and stem blocks, named by their commonest log id; spacing is the mean distance to the nearest tree of the same species within the same patch

underground.band: below surface - 8, down to the surface block's bottom

notable.common: minecraft:air, minecraft:andesite, minecraft:bedrock, minecraft:cave_air, minecraft:deepslate, minecraft:diorite, minecraft:dirt, minecraft:end_stone, minecraft:granite, minecraft:grass_block, minecraft:gravel, minecraft:netherrack, minecraft:sand, minecraft:stone, minecraft:tuff, minecraft:void_air, minecraft:water

clusters.method: 26-connected clusters of one notable block within a patch; spacing is the mean horizontal distance between cluster centres to the nearest in the same patch; a block in only one patch is not reported here

census.note: sites from the structure placement over the 1024-block border whose biome at the chunk centre takes the structure (terrain checks not applied; a set's site counts for its first such structure); distances from spawn (0, -64); byRing bounds [205, 410, 614, 819, 1024] blocks

biomeExpression.method: placement shares are % of the biome's own surface columns (plus sky-island tops); flags: mostly water or lava (but for a sea or river biome) or void (50%+; over a void-natured dimension, the End or sky islands, a biome is judged on its own surface columns and void is no flag), mostly bare rock (50%+ of land, but for a biome whose surface rule lays rock), a snowing climate (50%+) under 5% snow cover, a biome whose placed features are named for trees with none on a quarter hectare or more of its land; judged from 100+ columns

places.method: per layer, 16x16 cells described by numeric features (Gower-scaled to each feature's own 5th-95th percentile range) and categorical ones; k-medoids with k by the best silhouette (2-8, one type under 0.15); landmarks are cells farther from their medoid than both the 95th percentile and twice the median

vista.note: the coarse map's highest land cell and the point 160 blocks off in the direction of its largest drop

placeness.note: over the coarse map (8-block cells, 256 a side); regions are 4-connected cells of one surface biome or one landform class; edge cells lie within 64 blocks of a region boundary; correlation length is the semivariogram range (95% of the variance) along x and z

landBiomeRegions.note: regions of one biome over land cells outside a sea biome; shares and densities are of those cells, and only a boundary between two of them is an edge

islands.note: 4-connected land cells of the coarse map (8-block cells), specks included; dominantBiomePercent is the area-weighted mean share of each island's land in its own commonest biome

layerMaps.layout: patches tiled in plan order, 2 px a block, 2 px gaps; the legend is in the dossier
